facts.statement: Massaliasuchus is an extinct genus of allodaposuchid eusuchian crocodyliform found in the Late Cretaceous Fuvelian Lignites of southeastern France.
facts.quote: Massaliasuchus is an extinct monospecific genus of allodaposuchid eusuchian crocodyliform from the Late Cretaceous (Santonian–Campanian) Fuvelian Lignites of southeastern France.

facts.statement: Massaliasuchus was first described in 1869 by Philippe Matheron based on skull bones originally named Crocodilus affuvelensis.
facts.quote: Massaliasuchus was first described in 1869 by Philippe Matheron as Crocodilus affuvelensis, based on remains including skull bones.

facts.statement: The genus Massaliasuchus was renamed in 2008 by Jeremy Martin and Eric Buffetaut.
facts.quote: The new genus name was given to it in 2008 by Jeremy Martin and Eric Buffetaut.

facts.statement: Recent analysis classifies Massaliasuchus as a member of Allodaposuchidae, a group of basal eusuchians from the Late Cretaceous of southern Europe.
facts.quote: Recent cladistic analysis places Massaliasuchus as a member of Allodaposuchidae, a clade of basal eusuchians from the Late Cretaceous of southern Europe.

facts.statement: Massaliasuchus lived between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago during the Campanian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Massaliasuchus can be distinguished from Musturzabalsuchus by having 15 alveoli in the dentary bone.
facts.quote: The genus can be distinguished from Musturzabalsuchus in having 15 alveoli in the dentary.

facts.statement: Massaliasuchus is often omitted from phylogenetic analyses because it is known only from poorly preserved material.
facts.quote: However, Massaliasuchus is usually omitted from phylogenetic analyses since it is only represented by poorly-preserved material.
